mission_05: Speaker diarization is the task of determining who spoke when in an audio recording, answering the question who spoke when. It is a crucial preprocessing step for multi-party conversation analysis, meeting transcription, and broadcast news processing. The standard approach extracts speaker embeddings (x-vectors) from short audio segments, computes pairwise similarity between embeddings, and clusters segments to assign speaker labels. X-vectors are compact representations that capture speaker identity by training a time-delay neural network with a statistics pooling layer and a fully connected embedding layer. The similarity matrix is computed using cosine similarity between normalized embeddings. Spectral clustering transforms the similarity matrix into a low-dimensional embedding using the eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian, then applies k-means in this embedding space. The number of speakers can be estimated automatically using the eigenvalue gap heuristic. The Diarization Error Rate (DER) measures the percentage of time that is incorrectly assigned, computed by finding the optimal mapping between hypothesis and reference speaker labels. In this mission, you will implement the complete diarization pipeline from x-vector extraction through spectral clustering to error evaluation.
